set.approach: From the Big Sandy trailhead, near 9,000 ft, take the Big Sandy trail (trail 99) past Big Sandy Lake and North Lake toward Jackass Pass; it is roughly 9 miles to Lonesome Lake. Above North Lake the trail steepens, and a cairned spur to the left leads toward Arrowhead Lake and the cirque, while the main trail crosses Jackass Pass (about 10,800 ft) and drops steeply to Lonesome Lake. Cross the cirque to Pingora's south shoulder, reached by a well-worn trail on the shoulder's west side; two short branches cut right onto the shoulder, class 3 at most. Scramble up the ledges of the shoulder, class 3 to 4, until the rock steepens; the route starts there at a right-facing corner system.

review.notes: Trail and shoulder approach from the two Mountain Project route pages; pass height and distance from the Wikipedia cirque page and a trip write-up (distance given as a rounded figure). Descent already stored.

set.descent_text: From the summit, scramble over and down the third-class gully on the south side to the top of the K Cracks on South Buttress. The standard way off is the South Buttress rappel line, which starts at the anchors at the top of the K Cracks and runs down climber's left of the route in three or four rappels of roughly 25 to 32 m. A single 70 m rope reaches the ledges, two ropes work as well, and a 60 m rope needs some easy low-fifth-class downclimbing, so watch the rope ends. From the lowest anchors, walk the broad ledge left to the south shoulder; there is a short class 2-3 section just before it.
set.approach: From the Big Sandy trailhead, near 9,000 ft, take the Big Sandy trail (trail 99) past Big Sandy Lake and North Lake toward Jackass Pass; it is roughly 9 miles to Lonesome Lake. Above North Lake the trail steepens, and a cairned spur to the left leads toward Arrowhead Lake and the cirque, while the main trail crosses Jackass Pass (about 10,800 ft) and drops steeply to Lonesome Lake. For the northeast face, follow the trails on the north side of Lonesome Lake, keep left of the stream into the boulder field, then scramble left. Keep left of the foot of the curving ledge that turns into a long dihedral below a roof, gear up on the easy slabs, and go left up the third-class ramp to the first pitch.

review.notes: Face approach and descent gully from the Northeast Face page; rappel details agree across the South Buttress, East Face and area pages.

set.descent_text: From the top, scramble to the South Buttress rappel anchors at the top of the K Cracks. The standard way off is the South Buttress rappel line, which starts at the anchors at the top of the K Cracks and runs down climber's left of the route in three or four rappels of roughly 25 to 32 m. A single 70 m rope reaches the ledges, two ropes work as well, and a 60 m rope needs some easy low-fifth-class downclimbing, so watch the rope ends. From the lowest anchors, walk the broad ledge left to the south shoulder; there is a short class 2-3 section just before it. A party that bails when level with the south shoulder, just before the climbing kicks up again around pitches 6 to 8, can scramble around to the left onto the shoulder instead.
set.approach: From the Big Sandy trailhead, near 9,000 ft, take the Big Sandy trail (trail 99) past Big Sandy Lake and North Lake toward Jackass Pass; it is roughly 9 miles to Lonesome Lake. Above North Lake the trail steepens, and a cairned spur to the left leads toward Arrowhead Lake and the cirque, while the main trail crosses Jackass Pass (about 10,800 ft) and drops steeply to Lonesome Lake. The route is on Pingora's east side, just past the corner of the south shoulder. A snow patch marks the spot; the climbing begins to its right, in the rightmost of the parallel, left-leaning cracks.

review.notes: Start and bail option from the route page; rappel line agrees with South Buttress page and area page.

set.descent_text: After the final traverse left across the huge slabs and around the southeast corner, go down the gully-ramp to the South Buttress rappel anchors. The standard way off is the South Buttress rappel line, which starts at the anchors at the top of the K Cracks and runs down climber's left of the route in three or four rappels of roughly 25 to 32 m. A single 70 m rope reaches the ledges, two ropes work as well, and a 60 m rope needs some easy low-fifth-class downclimbing, so watch the rope ends. From the lowest anchors, walk the broad ledge left to the south shoulder; there is a short class 2-3 section just before it. The other way down is to retrace the East Ledges, downclimbing with a rappel or two, but the rappel line is faster.

set.approach: From the Big Sandy trailhead, near 9,000 ft, take the Big Sandy trail (trail 99) past Big Sandy Lake and North Lake toward Jackass Pass; it is roughly 9 miles to Lonesome Lake. Above North Lake the trail steepens, and a cairned spur to the left leads toward Arrowhead Lake and the cirque, while the main trail crosses Jackass Pass (about 10,800 ft) and drops steeply to Lonesome Lake. The route is on the northeast face: use the trails on the north side of Lonesome Lake, go left of the stream into the boulder field and scramble to the foot of the face. Its first crack system is the next one over, right of the Daley route, with easy slabs and low-angle right-facing dihedrals in the first pitch.

review.notes: Descent by East Ledges is what the first-ascent account used; both options and rap details are on the area page. Approach to the face from the Northeast Face page.
